title: TBDIWSG: Jim Stanford on Trump Trade War & Canada's Response
description:
Thunder Bay & District Injured Workers Support Group presents Jim Stanford, Economist and Director of the Centre for Future Work.

Topic: The current state of the Trump trade war and what Canada needs to do to respond.

Jim Stanford is one of Canada's best-known economic commentators. He served for over 20 years as Economist and Director of Policy with Unifor, Canada's largest private-sector trade union (formerly the Canadian Auto Workers). He is quoted frequently in the print and broadcast media, and writes a regular column for the Toronto Star.

Jim is also the Harold Innis Industry Professor in Economics at McMaster University in Hamilton, Canada, and an Honorary Professor in the Department of Political Economy at the University of Sydney. He has also served for many years as a Research Associate and volunteer with the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives.

From 2016 through 2024, Jim also served as founding Director of the Australian Centre for Future Work.

title: TBDIWSG: Family Members Focus Group - Workplace Injury Impact
description:
Have you supported a loved one who has been off work for 3 months or longer due to a workplace injury or illness?

Lakehead University, the Thunder Bay & District Injured Workers Support Group, and EPID@Work invite family members of injured workers to participate in an in-person focus group to share their experiences and perspectives.

This research aims to better understand the emotional, financial, and day-to-day impacts workplace injuries and illnesses have on families — impacts that are too often overlooked.

**Who can participate?**
Family members (partners, spouses, parents, adult children, or close relatives) of workers who:
• Have had a workplace injury or illness, and
• Are currently off work or have been off work for 3+ months

**What's involved:**
• A 2-hour, guided group discussion
• Confidential and respectful environment
• Participants receive a $50 gift card
• Light dinner provided

📌 Future dates (including online options) are available if you cannot attend this session.

👉 To participate: Complete the survey linked on the flyer or scan the QR code

For more information, contact Steve at (807) 767-9633

Your voice matters. Families deserve to be heard.

title: TBDIWSG: Glenn Shore - US National Commission on State Workmen's Compensation Laws
description:
Thunder Bay & District Injured Workers Support Group presents Glenn Shore discussing the US National Commission on State Workmen's Compensation Laws (1972).

**Topic:**
In 1970, with the passage of the first federal Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA), there was an acknowledgement that state workers compensation systems were ineffective at injury prevention and that there was need for a federal OSH regulatory system to serve that purpose. The OSHA act included a section establishing a National Commission on State Workmen's Compensation Laws to "determine if such laws provide an adequate, prompt, and equitable system of compensation" for work related injury, illness and fatalities.

The Commission, appointed by then president Richard Nixon and comprised of representatives from business, labor, insurance, state WC programs, claimant and defense attorneys defined a purpose and role for the state programs, and evaluated whether the states were meeting that goal. The Commission concluded unanimously that primary responsibility for the program at the state level should be "conserved" but noting that if the states could not make significant improvement in their programs, that there may be a place for federal minimum standards, in the manner that the OSHA act allowed for state control only if the states were "least as effective as" the national program.

This presentation will discuss the Commission's work and what happened after the Report was finalized in 1972.

**About Glenn Shore:**
Glenn Shore is a Continuing Lecturer at UC Berkeley School of Public Health with teaching experience at Cal State Hayward, San Francisco State University, and Sacramento State University. He is a retired public policy and research analyst with the California State Department of Industrial Relations, Cal/OSHA, and Division of Workers' Compensation with more than 30 years of experience.

title: Justice for Migrant Workers: EI Class Action Certification Hearing
description:
Justice for Migrant Workers is showing solidarity with migrant workers demanding an end to Canada's theft of EI payments.

**Background:**
Since 1966, migrant workers from the Caribbean and Mexico have contributed billions into Canada's Employment Insurance coffers. Since 2008 it is estimated that migrant farm workers have contributed half a billion dollars with unequal access.

In times of crisis such as the recent Hurricane Melissa that ravaged the island of Jamaica, migrant workers were not able to apply for benefits despite their significant need to rebuild their lives after the total devastation that many migrant workers returned home to.

**The Hearing:**
Class action certification hearing to demand an end to Canada's theft of EI benefits and equal access for all (Palmer v. Attorney General of Canada).

**How to Participate:**
• In person at Osgoode Hall
• By Zoom (message Justice for Migrant Workers for details)

**Show Your Support:**
• Attend in person or by Zoom
• Share and sign the petition to demand fair access to EI for all
• Stay connected with J4MW for follow-ups

Migrant workers are organizing to fight back against Canada's unjust enrichment at their expense. It's time to demand an EI system where all workers who contributed receive equal access.

Zoom link: https://ca01web.zoom.us/j/69438728776?pwd=tR8HBfbbFMQMWAzBbAHHNUbbGWSyg

More info: https://www.facebook.com/groups/2258183409/

title: TBDIWSG: Professor Harry Glasbeek - Corporate Crime & Worker Rights
description:
Thunder Bay & District Injured Workers Support Group presents Professor Harry Glasbeek.

**About the Speaker:**
Harry Glasbeek is professor emeritus and Senior Scholar of Osgoode Hall Law School, York University. He has taught in both Australia and Canada and has written 140 articles and 12 books, including Between the Lines titles:
• Wealth by Stealth: Corporate Crime, Corporate Law, and the Perversion of Democracy
• Class Privilege: How Law Shelters Shareholders and Coddles Capitalism
• Capitalism: A Crime Story

Professor Glasbeek brings decades of expertise on corporate accountability, worker rights, and the legal structures that shape workplace safety and compensation systems.

title: TBDIWSG: Sarah Rhodes - Occupational Disease Recognition
description:
Thunder Bay & District Injured Workers Support Group presents Sarah Rhodes on Occupational Disease and the challenges of getting recognition.

**Topic:**
Understanding occupational diseases and navigating the complex process of getting proper recognition and compensation through the workers' compensation system.

**Key Areas:**
• What constitutes occupational disease
• Challenges in proving work-relatedness
• Medical evidence and documentation requirements
• Appeals and advocacy strategies
• Support resources available

This session is crucial for workers dealing with occupational diseases or supporting those who are.

title: TBDIWSG: Occupational Safety & Health - Mobile Labour Force
description:
Thunder Bay & District Injured Workers Support Group presents a session on Occupational Safety and Health and Canada's mobile labour force: Obstacles to regulatory effectiveness.

**Topic:**
Exploring the unique challenges and regulatory gaps affecting mobile workers, including:
• Safety challenges for workers who move between job sites
• Jurisdictional issues in regulation enforcement
• Barriers to effective health and safety oversight
• Rights and protections for mobile workers
• Advocacy and reform opportunities

This session examines the critical intersection of worker mobility, safety regulation, and effective enforcement.

title: Double Feature: 3mpwrApp Tech Demo + Workers' Rights with Jaribu Hill
description:
Pleased to invite you to an amazing double feature on March 31 at 10 AM ET on Zoom!

**PART 1: Tech for Collective Power (1 hour)**
Lissa Beaulieu, creator of 3mpwrApp, hosts an interactive presentation exploring how tech can transform isolated struggles into collective power. We'll dive deep into the 3 mechanism flywheels of change built into 3mpwrApp:
- Evidence Flywheel: Win your case while sharing knowledge
- Collective Action Flywheel: 50+ users = systemic change campaigns
- Knowledge Network Flywheel: AI and peer mentoring accelerate success

Live demo, current app status, and Q&A. Visit: https://3mpwrapp.pages.dev/

**PART 2: Civil and Human Rights Advocacy (1 hour)**
Jaribu Hill - Civil and Human Rights Attorney, Founder and Executive Director of the Mississippi Workers' Center for Human Rights. International spokesperson on Civil and Human Rights topics with experience across Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Caribbean. Attorney Hill has provided legal representation for hundreds of workers, led adoption of "Zero Tolerance Against Hate" policies, won judgment against the Ku Klux Klan in South Carolina, and assisted Mississippi Delta parents in their fight for school equity.

Contact us at tbiwsg@gmail.com to join this Zoom Session!
More info: https://thunderbayinjuredworkers.com/
organizer: Thunder Bay & District Injured Workers Support Group & 3mpwr App
